page: Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-intel is a High Performance virtual server featuring 12 shared vCPUs mapped to 6 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the x86_64 processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and includes 500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations place this server consistently in the average performance tier across standard workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1418.58 and a multi-core score of 17309.27, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 17934.88. Memory performance is characterized by a cached small-block read bandwidth of 1224.9 GB/sec, which drops to 87.74 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 47.62 GB/sec for writes. In application-specific tests, the instance demonstrates a static web serving throughput of 11.99 GB/sec and handles 18.53 million Redis SET operations per second.

Due to the shared CPU allocation, the instance is susceptible to resource contention under sustained, maximum CPU utilization, making it less suitable for continuous high-load compute tasks. This is reflected in its weak performance on larger computational tasks, such as medium 7B LLM inference, which yields only 7.43 tokens/sec for text generation. However, the server is well-suited for bursty workloads, software compilation, database operations, and web serving where the 500 GB NVMe SSD and 12 vCPUs can be leveraged efficiently without requiring dedicated CPU cores.

It features 24.0 GB of RAM and 500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard operations, with a PassMark CPU score of 17934.88 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 17309.27. The server delivers a static web serving throughput of 11.99 GB/sec and processes 18.53 million Redis SET operations per second. While the shared CPU allocation presents potential performance variability under sustained heavy loads, the instance offers a cost-effective balance of compute capacity and fast NVMe storage.
